locations.result: Read Overview; How it works; FAQ. AoE manages parallel persistent tmux sessions on Linux/macOS, with CLI/TUI/browser/API access, optional worktrees/containers, phone browser access and SSH reconnect. Windows is WSL2 only.

Read aoe add; send; ps; agents; acp. CLI creates, lists, sends to, forks and removes sessions. Custom commands and ACP agent/model/effort selection are supported; named resume/fork examples include Claude, Codex, OpenCode and Pi.

Read Launch; access modes; security. The shipped dashboard drives sessions from a browser; tmux and persistent structured workers survive browser crashes. Remote access supports authenticated tunnel modes and read-only views.
Read Session endpoints; MCP server. HTTP and typed MCP operations expose session management. Authentication and read-only restrictions vary by daemon launch mode.

Read Turn it on; Authentication; Limits. MCP control is opt-in, off by default; it exposes session operations under daemon credentials. It adds no per-tool permissions beyond the connected users access.
Read MCP forwarding. AoE forwards configured external MCP server definitions to launched agents, distinct from its inbound control MCP server.

Read Configuration; Private stores; Shared credentials. Optional Docker, Podman or Apple Container runs the agent with workspace mounts, resource/network configuration and per-session history stores. Claude refresh credentials are shared across sandbox sessions, with documented refresh conflicts.
Read Worktree creation and lifecycle. Git worktrees isolate session working copies/branches; they are separate from container security controls.

Read Managed contexts; Refusals. Resume/fork support depends on harness, store and OS. Codex with ChatGPT login is explicitly refused for managed resume/fork, and unsandboxed macOS Codex has additional limits.
Read Comparisons; Inline review. Diff UI supports comparison bases and line comments sent as follow-up prompts. Comments are localStorage per session and move to a stale block when code changes.
Read Defaults; Controls; Never sent. Anonymous telemetry is opt-in, off by default. aoe telemetry disable and DO_NOT_TRACK suppress sending; settings expose consent and reset controls.
Read MIT grant. AoE is MIT licensed, with an Apache-2.0-derived file separately disclosed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.
